## Conceptual background

rehydra follows the resistance-recovery-resilience framework and extends it with operational drought-memory metrics across repeated stress cycles.

## Data and preparation

```r
library(rehydra)
data(rehydra_data)

prepared <- prepare_rehydra_data(
  data = rehydra_data,
  time = time_days,
  genotype = genotype,
  treatment = treatment,
  replicate = replicate,
  variables = c(water_potential, stomatal_conductance),
  response_direction = "auto"
)
```

## Segmentation

```r
segments <- segment_drought_cycle(
  data = prepared,
  time = time,
  value = transformed_value,
  method = "auto"
)
```

## Resistance, recovery, and resilience

```r
resilience <- resilience_index(segments)
head(resilience)
```

## Damage and recovery dynamics

```r
damage <- damage_metrics(segments)
recovery <- recovery_metrics(segments)
```

## Memory effects

```r
memory <- memory_effect(
  resilience_results = resilience,
  damage_results = damage,
  recovery_results = recovery,
  cycle_ref = 1,
  cycle_test = 2
)

classification <- priming_classification(memory)
head(classification)
```

## Memory across three or more cycles

`memory_effect()` compares two cycles at a time. When the experiment imposed
several cycles, `memory_trend()` fits the whole sequence and returns the memory
rate: the average change in the index per additional cycle.

```r
trend <- memory_trend(resilience, min_cycles = 2)
trend[, c("genotype", "metric", "slope", "p_value", "monotonic_fraction",
          "memory_class")]
```

`monotonic_fraction` is the proportion of consecutive cycle-to-cycle steps that
move with the slope. A significant slope with a fraction near `0.5` is driven by
the endpoints rather than by a consistent progression.

The same trend can be fitted on the curve-shape indices, where a *falling* value
means an improvement; `memory_trend()` flips the direction automatically, so
`"acquired_memory"` always means the plant coped better in the later cycles.

```r
shape <- curve_shape_metrics(segments)
memory_trend(shape, metrics = c("deficit_auc_normalized", "t50"), min_cycles = 2)
```

## Testing the indices in the experimental design

```r
fit <- rehydra_anova(resilience, response = "Rs",
                     factors = c("genotype", "treatment"))
fit$anova
fit$means
fit$comparisons
```

## Genotype comparison

```r
comparison <- compare_genotypes(resilience, metric = "Rs")
comparison$pairwise
```

## Key visual summaries

```r
plot_resilience_indices(resilience)
plot_memory_effect(memory)
plot_damage_recovery(damage, recovery)
plot_memory_trend(resilience, trend)
```
